headline: AI mistakes lead 85% of companies to cut humans from testing
summary: Despite rising trust in automated AI evaluation, nearly half of companies report AI features passing tests only to fail in production, prompting a shift away from human oversight.
details: New research reveals a concerning trend: companies that have experienced AI failures in production are increasingly removing humans from the testing and deployment process, rather than enhancing oversight.

A recent VB Pulse survey found that while trust in automated AI evaluation has risen significantly, 49% of enterprises reported that an AI agent or LLM-powered feature that cleared company testing subsequently caused a customer-facing problem. This figure remained largely unchanged from the previous month.

Alarmingly, nearly a quarter of these companies (24%) stated that such a failure had occurred more than once. This indicates a growing gap between confidence in automated evaluation systems and their actual effectiveness in preventing real-world issues.

The findings suggest that as AI systems become more complex, enumerating all potential failure cases becomes impossible. Consequently, companies are shifting their focus from traditional evaluation sets to anomaly and issue detection solutions.

Industry experts note a 'great decline of evals as we know them,' with major corporations deprioritizing maintenance and reducing eval sets. The market is rapidly transforming, with solutions focused on post-production monitoring gaining traction.

This shift is driven by the realization that even AI systems that pass rigorous internal testing can fail when exposed to the complexities of live production environments. The data indicates a need for more robust, real-world testing and monitoring strategies.
